title: Getting Started with cdfquant01reg
text: two commands executing regression model, one identifying distribution used regression model, specifying regression model data source. select_ftcdfq() command displays menu 32 FTCDFQ distributions asks number identifying distribution chosen user. function print 32 standard distribution options prompt choice: enter number (e.g., 3), custom Stan variables registered automatically, see message like one: package handles BRMS custom family stanvars automatically, ftcdfq command running model needs BRMS formula data source, although BRMS control parameters can added well (e.g., number chains). example executes intercepts model using two-parameter distribution dependent variable pphysdecis dataset named “yoon” (Example 3 Smithson Shou, 2024, see description dataset). BRMS post-estimation functions commands available, log_lik epred. Also available estimates conditional pdf, cdf, quantile functions distribution employed regression model. commands dnsity, CDF, inverse_CDF, respectively. Given model , following commands produce model distribution’s median cdf three points. commands use dnsity function plot fitted distribution normed histogram data.
code: # Run the interactive menu selection select_ftcdfq() Choose a BRMS model to load into the session:    1: Arcsinh_Arcsinh_outer_W_2   2: Arcsinh_Cauchy_outer_W_2    3: Cauchit_Arcsinh_outer_W_2 ... 31: Cauchit_Cauchy_inner_V_3   32: t2_t2_inner_V_3  Selection: Selection: 3 --> --> Successfully loaded: Cauchit_Arcsinh_outer_W_2 The shared and unique Stan functions are now active. data(yoon) # Run the model m1 <- ftcdfq(bf(pphysdecis ~ 1, sigma ~ 1), data=yoon, backend = "cmdstanr") # Get the model summary summary(m1) # Get the model coefficients: b0 <- fixef(m1)["Intercept", "Estimate"] s0 <- exp(fixef(m1)["sigma_Intercept", "Estimate"]) # Compute the estimated median: inverse_CDF(0.5,b0,s0) # Compare it with the sample median: median(yoon$pphysdecis) # Inspect the CDF values for 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 on the pphysdecis scale: c(CDF(0.25,b0,s0),CDF(0.5,b0,s0),CDF(0.75,b0,s0)) library(MASS) # Draw the fitted distribution and histogram myseq <- seq(0,1,0.01) mydensity <- c(rep(0,length(myseq))) for (i in 1:length(mydensity)) {mydensity[i] <- dnsity(myseq[i],b0,s0)} truehist(yoon$pphysdecis, nbins=50, xlab = "pphysdecis", ylab = "pdf") lines(myseq,mydensity, lwd = 2)

title: Getting Started with cdfquant01reg
text: data records 894 patients whose times recorded five stages ED assessment treatment study consisting recorded information patients admitted emergency department University Alberta Hospital midnight January 23 midnight January 29, 1999 (Yoon, Steiner, Reinhardt 2003). Smithson Shou used Cauchit-Cauchy outer-W two-parameter distribution assess difference proportion time spent treatment (versus registration triage) patients arriving ambulance “walk-ins”. code tests hypothesis ambulance-arrivals spent time treatment physician, using Cauchit-Arcsinh outer-W distribution already employed vignette. next code chunk draws fitted distributions histograms walk-ins ambulance-arrivals.
code: # Run the model m2 <- ftcdfq(bf(pphysdecis ~ Ambulance, sigma ~ Ambulance), data=yoon, backend = "cmdstanr") # Get the model summary summary(m2) # Get the model log-likelihood: LL1 <- log_lik(m1) sum(colMeans(LL1)) #  # Get the model estimated medians for the Walk-ins b0 <- fixef(m2)["Intercept", "Estimate"] s0 <- exp(fixef(m2)["sigma_Intercept", "Estimate"]) inverse_CDF(0.5,b0,s0) # Compare it with the sample median: median(yoon$pphysdecis[yoon$Ambulance==0]) # # And for the Ambulance Arrivals: b1 <- fixef(m2)["Ambulance", "Estimate"] s1 <- exp(fixef(m2)["sigma_Ambulance", "Estimate"]) inverse_CDF(0.5,b0+b1,s0+s1) # Compare it with the sample median: median(yoon$pphysdecis[yoon$Ambulance==1]) # Draw the fitted distribution and histogram for the Walk-ins myseq <- seq(0,1,0.01) mydensity <- c(rep(0,length(myseq))) for (i in 1:length(mydensity)) {mydensity[i] <- dnsity(myseq[i],b0,s0)} truehist(yoon$pphysdecis[yoon$Ambulance == 0], nbins=50, xlab = "pphysdecis", ylab = "pdf") lines(myseq,mydensity, lwd = 2) # # Draw the fitted distribution and histogram for the Ambulance Arrivals for (i in 1:length(mydensity)) {mydensity[i] <- dnsity(myseq[i],b0+b1,s0+s1)} truehist(yoon$pphysdecis[yoon$Ambulance == 1], nbins=50, xlab = "pphysdecis", ylab = "pdf") lines(myseq,mydensity, lwd = 2)

title: Getting Started with cdfquant01reg
text: section describes regression modeling extended-support FTCDFQ distributions. , two commands executing regression model, one identifying distribution used regression model, specifying regression model data source. select_exftcdfq() command displays menu 16 extended-support FTCDFQ distributions asks number identifying distribution chosen user. function print 16 extended-support distribution options prompt choice: , enter number (e.g., 1), custom Stan variables registered automatically, see message like one: example first executes intercepts model using selected distribution dependent variable ptotpalest1 dataset named “blame” (see description dataset). u_Intercept model summary logged exceedance parameter, amount unit interval extended 1 0 handle zeros ones data.
code: # Run the interactive menu selection select_exftcdfq() Choose a BRMS model to load into the session:    1: Ex_Arcsinh_Arcsinh_outer_W   2: Ex_Arcsinh_Cauchy_outer_W      ...  15: Ex_Cauchit_Cauchy_inner_V   16: Ex_t2_t2_inner_V  Selection: Selection: 1 --> Successfully loaded: Ex_Arcsinh_Arcsinh_outer_W The shared and unique Stan functions are now active. data(blame) # Run the model m3 <- exftcdfq(bf(ptotpalest1 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1, u ~ 1), data= blame) # Get the model summary summary(m3) # Get the model log-likelihood: LL3 <- log_lik(m3) sum(colMeans(LL3)) # # model distribution’s median: b0 <- fixef(m1)["Intercept", "Estimate"] s0 <- exp(fixef(m1)["sigma_Intercept", "Estimate"]) u0 <- exp(fixef(m1)["u_Intercept", "Estimate"]) inverse_CDF(0.5,b0,s0,u0) # Compare the estimate with the empirical median: median(blame$ptotpalest1) #

title: Getting Started with cdfquant01reg
text: data example replication extension Halevy et al. (2022), replication conducted Smithson. Israeli adult sample recruited using Qualtrics panel platform April 2021 (N = 462; mean age = 39.9, age SD = 15.5; 245 females, 214 males, 3 ). participants asked assign percentages blame Israelis Palestinians unresolved Israeli-Palestinian conflict: “present, permanent solution Israeli-Palestinian conflict yet found. blame current absence permanent solution? table find two groups. Please indicate much think blame absence permanent solution conflict. Please note – total sum percentages must add 100%.” Two experimental conditions varied whether Palestinians listed one population “unpacked” three separate movements: Palestinians listed “Palestinians” vs listed “Palestinian Hamas movement, Palestinian Fatah movement, Palestinian Islamic Jihad movement”. hypothesis tested unpacking three groups increase percentage blame Israeli participants assigned Palestinians. regression model shows support hypothesis. palestpk variable coded 0 (unpacked) 1 (packed). positive effect palestpk skew parameter implies unpacked condition yielded higher median packed condition.
code: # Run the model m4 <- exftcdfq(bf(ptotpalest1 ~ palestpk, sigma ~ 1, u ~ 1), data= blame) # Get the model summary summary(m4) #  # Get the model log-likelihood: LL4 <- log_lik(m4) sum(colMeans(LL4)) # # Get the model estimated medians for the “unpacked” condition b0 <- fixef(m2)["Intercept", "Estimate"] s0 <- exp(fixef(m2)["sigma_Intercept", "Estimate"]) u0 <- exp(fixef(m2)["u_Intercept", "Estimate"]) inverse_CDF(0.5,b0,s0,u0) # Compare the estimate with the empirical median: median(blame$ptotpalest1[blame$palestpk==0]) # # And for the “packed” condition: b1 <- fixef(m2)["palestpk", "Estimate"] inverse_CDF(0.5,b0+b1,s0,u0) # Compare the estimate with the empirical median: median(blame$ptotpalest1[blame$palestpk==1]) #  # Draw the fitted distribution and histogram for the “packed” myseq <- seq(-u0,1+u0,0.01) mydensity <- c(rep(0,length(myseq))) for (i in 1:length(mydensity)) {mydensity[i] <- dnsity(myseq[i],b0,s0,u0)} truehist(blame$ptotpalest1[blame$palestpk == 0], nbins=20, xlab = "ptotpalest1", ylab = "pdf", xlim = c(-u0,1+u0)) lines(myseq,mydensity, lwd = 2) # # Draw the fitted distribution and histogram for the “unpacked” for (i in 1:length(mydensity)) {mydensity[i] <- dnsity(myseq[i],b0+b1,s0,u0)} truehist(blame$ptotpalest1[blame$palestpk == 1], nbins=20, xlab = "ptotpalest1", ylab = "pdf", xlim = c(-u0,1+u0)) lines(myseq,mydensity, lwd = 2)
